hero.h1: It is going to be done
hero.lede: Already decided, already in motion, and the decider is nowhere in the sentence. This is the one you meet in the letter that tells you what is about to happen to your street, your contract or your account.

sections.label: Descent briefing
sections.title: When to use it
sections.lead: The passive is not a different tense. It is the going to future with the doer let go — and the reason you let them go is always one of these six.

cards.head: You do not know who
cards.body: Nobody can tell you the doer, so the sentence does without one.

cards.head: The doer does not matter
cards.body: The event is the news; who did it is a footnote.

cards.head: The doer is obvious
cards.body: Saying it would be a waste of everyone's time.

cards.head: You would rather not say
cards.body: The passive is how English removes a person from a sentence.
cards.ex: "Some of these posts are going to be cut."

cards.head: Putting the important thing first
cards.body: Whatever you put at the front is what the sentence is about.
cards.ex: "The whole street is going to be resurfaced."

cards.head: Putting the doer back with by
cards.body: When the doer is the point, it goes at the end.
cards.ex: "The work is going to be done by the council."

cards.head: Affirmative
cards.body: subject + am / is / are + going to be + past participle

cards.head: Negative
cards.body: the not goes after the first auxiliary

cards.head: Questions
cards.body: the first auxiliary moves to the front

cards.head: With the doer
cards.ex: "It is going to be done by the council."

charts.head: Turning an active sentence around
charts.note: Three moves, always the same: the object comes to the front, the verb becomes am / is / are + going to be + participle, and the old subject either disappears or goes to the back behind by. Only the middle step changes from camp to camp.

head: Active
Passive
What moved
rows: They are going to demolish the shop.
The shop is going to be demolished.
The shop came first.
Someone is going to charge him.
He is going to be charged.
Someone said nothing.
The council is going to do the work.
The work is going to be done by the council.
The council stayed, at the end.
They are going to cut some posts.
Some posts are going to be cut.
Plural subject, so are.

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Four words in a fixed order — going, to, be, participle — and only am, is or are in front of them ever changes.

head: Subject
Affirmative
Negative
Question
rows: It
It is going to be done
It isn't going to be done
Is it going to be done?
They
They are going to be done
They aren't going to be done
Are they going to be done?
I
I am going to be moved
I'm not going to be moved
Am I going to be moved?
You
You are going to be asked
You aren't going to be asked
Are you going to be asked?
We
We are going to be told
We aren't going to be told
Are we going to be told?

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this one is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: The shop is going to be demolish.
The shop is going to be demolished.
After be comes the participle, every time.
The shop is going be demolished.
The shop is going to be demolished.
The to is part of the form and cannot be dropped.
The shop will going to be demolished.
The shop is going to be demolished.
Pick one future. Will and going to do not stack.

charts.note: Neither is better. The question is only what the sentence is about — because whatever you put at the front is what the reader will think it is about.

head: Question
Passive
Active
rows: What is the sentence about?

The thing it happens to.
"The shop is going to be demolished."

The one who does it.
"They are going to demolish the shop."
Do you know the doer?
Often not — and you do not need to.
Yes, and you are naming them.
Where does the doer go?
At the end with by, or nowhere at all.
At the front, as the subject.
Which is shorter?
Longer by two or three words.
Usually shorter. Prefer it when both work.

charts.example: Camp five is the tense of things already decided, and in the passive that is exactly what makes it uncomfortable to read: your contract is going to be reviewed tells you the decision has been taken and declines to say by whom. The evidence is there; the decider is not.

sections.title: Signal words

signals.head: Verbs with no passive at all

sections.example: The test for whether a verb can go passive: does it take an object? They built it has one, so it turns. It happened has none, so it cannot.

sections.title: The event, and the doer you dropped

diagram.intro: The block is the same block as the ascent, lit from above instead of fading into the dark — because the tense has not changed, only the light. Inside it sits a dashed box: the doer. It is drawn inside the event rather than beside it because the doer is not a moment in time, it is a part of the sentence — and it is dashed because most of the time nobody says it. Click either to see it in a sentence.

panels.head: The event — now the subject
items: The shop is going to be demolished.
Some of these posts are going to be cut.

panels.head: The doer — optional, and usually gone
items: … and nobody at all is cutting them.

quiz.explain: Is + going to be + participle. Is going to demolish would make the shop the demolisher.
Is going to be widened. Will and going to never stack.
Posts is plural, so are, and cut is its own participle.
The not goes after is, and the rest of the chain follows unchanged.
Is + subject + going to be + participle.
Do / did / done. The doer goes at the end behind by.
By the police goes without saying, so the passive drops it.
I takes am, and being moved is something that happens to you.
Last year is a finished past time, so the past simple passive.
Are going to be told. Tell / told / told.
Is going to be reviewed — the decision is taken and the decider is missing.
Nothing is singular and is not doing the changing.

quiz.prompt: Two hundred trees _____ along the new road. (plant)
quiz.explain: Trees is plural, so are going to be planted.
Street is singular, so is, and the participle resurfaced.

results: Clean run. You can turn a sentence around and you know when the doer is worth keeping.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at the active version before you go on.
Good first attempt. The auxiliary chain is the part to read again.
